title: AEO Engine turned an old Amazon ad agency into a $204K month by renaming itself for the AI search wave
dek: It did not start from zero. An Amazon marketing agency from 2018 re-launched as an 'answer engine' agency in January 2026, just as brands started asking how to show up in ChatGPT. Its MRR (monthly recurring revenue: what clients pay every month) is $190,513, read straight from Stripe. A month's revenue is the money actually collected that month, so it doesn't match MRR exactly.

cost_to_start.text: $1,000, as told to a founder-story site.
cost_to_start.label: Claimed

first_revenue.text: Not public. The business says its roots go back to an Amazon marketing agency started in 2018, so it already had paying clients before the AEO Engine name.
first_revenue.label: Claimed

first_customers.text: Not public. The company says the older agency served 100+ Amazon and Shopify brands, and the team is closely tied to Amazon seller communities and events.

phases.name: An Amazon agency
phases.story: The business began as FosterFBA, which helped people sell on Amazon. FBA means Fulfilled by Amazon: Amazon stores and ships the seller's products. In January 2019 its homepage offered product research, listing optimization and free tools. By 2023 it called itself a 'Data Driven Amazon Advertising Agency' and offered a free audit to get calls booked.

number.v: "Research, Optimize & Scale your Amazon FBA Business"
number.label: Wayback

phases.lesson: A small service business can run for years and build skills you can carry into the next thing.

phases.name: Spotting the new search
phases.story: People started asking ChatGPT and Google's AI answers instead of clicking search results. The company says it was already doing AI search work through 2025. By October 2025 aeoengine.ai was live, promising to get brands 'featured in ChatGPT, Google AI & Perplexity answers' and offering a free audit.
phases.lesson: When the way people search changes, the people who already know the old way have a head start on the new one.

phases.name: A new name
phases.story: The company says it 'formalized' the AEO Engine brand around January 2026. AEO means answer engine optimization: making sure an AI recommends you when someone asks a question. It is like SEO (getting found on Google), but for AI answers. That month a founder-story site listed it at $65,000 a month, which matches the Stripe numbers.
phases.lesson: A clear name for what you do can matter as much as the work itself.

phases.name: Showing up everywhere
phases.story: In March 2026 it started a podcast about AI search, now billed as a daily show. In April the founder gave the AEO talk at a big Amazon seller conference in Nashville, where the agency's old clients gather. Revenue jumped to $98K in March, then settled around $75K to $77K a month.
phases.lesson: Go where your existing customers already are and teach them something new.

phases.name: The jump
phases.story: Revenue went from about $80K in August to $164K in September and $204K in October. Plans are public: $1,597 or $2,997 a month, or custom from $10,000. In November it published an 'Answer Index' ranking how visible 100 law firms are in AI answers. We couldn't find a public reason for the September jump.
phases.lesson: Public prices and free reports let buyers say yes faster.

checklist: Write down one skill you already have (editing, design, a game, a sport) and one new tool or trend it connects to.
Ask ChatGPT a question your favourite local shop's customers would ask, and see whether the shop shows up in the answer.
Make a free one-page 'audit' you could give a business, like a list of 5 fixes for their Instagram or website.
Pick one place your target customers already gather (a Discord, a club, a subreddit) and post one useful tip there.
Put a real price on your offer before anyone asks, even if it's small.
Rank 10 local businesses on one thing you can check (reviews, menu online, opening hours right) and share the list.
